article_title: Daily affective-motivational experiences during exam preparation: Feedback loops, stability, and change over time.
citation: Berweger, B., Breitwieser, J., Kracke, B., Brod, G., & Dietrich, J. (2024). Daily Affective-Motivational Experiences During Exam Preparation: Feedback Loops, Stability, and Change Over Time. PsychArchives preprint. https://hdl.handle.net/20.500.12034/10953
title: 40-day daily diary study of medical students' affective-motivational experiences during exam preparation
description: This element is the study design through which the article generates its evidence: "This study examined daily feedback loops and fluctuations in medical students’ affective-motivational experiences during a 40-day exam preparation period." Motivational states were operationalized as cognitive appraisals of daily goals and self-efficacy, and emotional states as the achievement emotions joy, pride, anxiety, anger, and boredom. The repeated daily measures were analyzed with Dynamic Structural Equation Modeling in Mplus to detect feedback loops and stability of experiences within and between learning sessions.
requirements: Repeated daily self-reports of cognitive appraisals, self-efficacy, and achievement emotions across the preparation period, analyzed with DSEM in Mplus
constraints: The manuscript is a preprint that has not been certified by peer review and is currently under review
target_learning_goals: tracking motivation and achievement emotions during self-regulated learning
examples: Daily reports collected across a 40-day exam preparation period were modeled with DSEM to identify feedback loops within and between learning sessions
key_sources: Berweger, B., Breitwieser, J., Kracke, B., Brod, G., & Dietrich, J. (2024). Daily Affective-Motivational Experiences During Exam Preparation: Feedback Loops, Stability, and Change Over Time. PsychArchives preprint. https://hdl.handle.net/20.500.12034/10953

article_title: Assessing the Effectiveness of STAD Model and Problem Based Learning in Mathematics Learning Achievement and Problem Solving Ability
citation: Tawachai Rattanatumma and Dr.Vichian Puncreobutr. (2016). Assessing the Effectiveness of STAD Model and Problem Based Learning in Mathematics Learning Achievement and Problem Solving Ability. Journal of Education and Practice, Vol.7, No.12. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1105110
title: 40-item multiple choice pre-test and post-test instrument for mathematics learning achievement and problem solving ability
description: The researchers created 40 multiple choice questions with 4 choices to assess the Mathematics Learning Achievement and the Problem Solving Ability of the students. This instrument was administered as a pre-test during orientation and again as a post-test after the 16-hour instructional period, providing the outcome measures analyzed via ANCOVA.
requirements: Administered before instruction as a pre-test and after instruction as a post-test
constraints: Content based on the curriculum of Bachelor Degree in Mathematics in accordance with the Office of the Higher Education Commission
examples: The instrument was used with two groups of 25 students each in the first semester of Academic Year 2015.
key_sources: Tawachai Rattanatumma and Dr.Vichian Puncreobutr. (2016). Assessing the Effectiveness of STAD Model and Problem Based Learning in Mathematics Learning Achievement and Problem Solving Ability. Journal of Education and Practice, Vol.7, No.12. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1099565

article_title: The Effect of Using Video Technology on Improving Reading Comprehension of Iranian Intermediate EFL Learners
citation: Amir Mohammadian, Amin Saed, Younes Shahi. (2018). The Effect of Using Video Technology on Improving Reading Comprehension of Iranian Intermediate EFL Learners. Advances in Language and Literary Studies, 9(2). https://doi.org/10.7575/aiac.alls.v.9n.2p.17
title: 40-item multiple-choice reading comprehension pre-test and post-test
description: The study's outcome instrument was a 40-item multiple-choice reading comprehension test, administered as both pre-test and post-test with identical items and scoring: "one mark for recognizing each test item correctly and zero for incorrect recognition", giving a maximum score of 40. It was used to establish group equivalence before treatment and to compare groups afterward.
requirements: Administered to both groups before and after the treatment to assess reading comprehension ability.
target_learners: intermediate EFL learners in secondary school
target_learning_goals: reading comprehension in English as a foreign language
examples: Pre-test means of 18.73 (control) and 19.07 (experimental) and post-test means of 19.80 and 23.80 were computed from this instrument.
key_sources: Amir Mohammadian, Amin Saed, Younes Shahi. (2018). The Effect of Using Video Technology on Improving Reading Comprehension of Iranian Intermediate EFL Learners. Advances in Language and Literary Studies, 9(2). https://doi.org/10.7575/aiac.alls.v.9n.2p.17

article_title: Improving diagnostic and management competencies for common orofacial conditions among new dental graduates: the effect of an educational intervention.
citation: Aljohani Suad, Alhamed Sana, Farag Arwa M, Aljohani Salha R, Jazzar Ahoud, AlDehlawi Hebah, Almohammadi Abdullah, Alghamdi Malik, Aljohani Khalid. (2026). Improving diagnostic and management competencies for common orofacial conditions among new dental graduates: the effect of an educational intervention. BMC Oral Health. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12903-026-07662-7
title: Validated 40-item case-based questionnaire with 20 clinical scenarios assessing diagnostic and management competency
description: An online Google Forms questionnaire of 40 multiple-choice questions based on 20 clinical scenarios, each scenario pairing a clinical image with one diagnostic and one management question. Content was reviewed by four oral medicine consultants, and test-retest reliability on three pilot subjects produced a "weighted κ = 0.937 (95% CI: 0.877–0.996)". It was administered at baseline, immediately post-lecture, and two months later.
requirements: Clinical scenarios with keywords relevant to condition characteristics and a clear representative clinical image
Review by oral medicine consultants for content and face validity
constraints: Test-retest validation used only three pilot subjects, which the authors state limits generalizability of the reliability results
target_learning_goals: Management planning for common oral lesions
examples: Administered to 161 dental interns at baseline with 91 completing all three stages
key_sources: Aljohani Suad, Alhamed Sana, Farag Arwa M, Aljohani Salha R, Jazzar Ahoud, AlDehlawi Hebah, Almohammadi Abdullah, Alghamdi Malik, Aljohani Khalid. (2026). Improving diagnostic and management competencies for common orofacial conditions among new dental graduates: the effect of an educational intervention. BMC Oral Health. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12903-026-07662-7

article_title: Integrated e-Learning for Shoulder Anatomy and Clinical Examination Skills in First-Year Medical Students: Randomized Controlled Trial.
citation: Koch R, Gassner L, Gerlach N, Festl-Wietek T, Hirt B, Joos S, Shiozawa T. (2025). Integrated e-Learning for Shoulder Anatomy and Clinical Examination Skills in First-Year Medical Students: Randomized Controlled Trial. JMIR Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.2196/62666
title: 40-item video-based shoulder examination checklist with blinded dual rating
description: A standardized 40-item examination checklist used to score uploaded videos of students performing shoulder examinations on volunteer simulation patients. It comprises "12 items on anatomical knowledge, such as topography and functional anatomy, 17 items on structured clinical examination skills, and 9 items on medical professionalism," developed in multidisciplinary workshops from existing literature and the UKT OSCE. Videos were limited to 10 minutes and rated independently by a blinded GP and medical student pair; interrater reliability in the main study was 0.763 after items were re-operationalized following a pilot κ=0.573.
requirements: Blinded raters and standardized item operationalization
Volunteers without preexisting shoulder pain or functional impairments, with consent obtained
constraints: Used because contact restrictions prevented a face-to-face OSCE; the article presents videotaped examination as a viable alternative when face-to-face exams are not possible
examples: Videos uploaded to ILIAS were scored by two blinded raters; the checklist is included as Multimedia Appendix 1
key_sources: Koch R, Gassner L, Gerlach N, Festl-Wietek T, Hirt B, Joos S, Shiozawa T. (2025). Integrated e-Learning for Shoulder Anatomy and Clinical Examination Skills in First-Year Medical Students: Randomized Controlled Trial. JMIR Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.2196/62666

article_title: Effect of Training Program on Evidence-Based Practice Competencies in Hospital Nurses in Taiwan: A Quasi-Experimental Study.
citation: Yeh M.-L., Chang B.-Y., Dai H.-D., & Chung M.-H. (2025). Effect of training program on evidence-based practice competencies in hospital nurses in Taiwan: A quasi-experimental study. The Journal of Nursing Research, 33(5), e412. https://doi.org/10.1097/jnr.0000000000000701
title: 40-hour EBP training program combining lectures, hands-on practice, and mentored consultation
description: A 40-hour evidence-based practice training program for clinical nurses delivered over 2 weeks, built around the five EBP steps and the PICO format. It comprised "20 hours of face-to-face lectures, 10 hours of group and individual consulting, and 10 hours of hands-on training and participation in evidence-based campaigns and nursing conferences." Participants worked in four teams, "each team mentored by a well-trained, evidence-based nursing facilitator," with debriefing meetings after each class and consultation by appointment.
requirements: Instructors with nursing, medical, and statistics background as well as expertise in empirical research; facilitators able to guide article searches, interpretation, and solving technical difficulties in actual practice
constraints: Delivered and evaluated in a single Taiwanese hospital setting with a convenience sample; group allocation was not randomized but based on participant intentions
target_learners: currently practicing clinical nurses in hospitals
target_learning_goals: evidence-based practice competencies: asking clinical questions, acquiring and appraising research evidence, applying and assessing results, and addressing barriers and facilitators
examples: Lecture activities included self-reflection exercises and post-class debriefing meetings; practice sessions searched PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Medline and interpreted meta-analysis results; each facilitator consulted with 10 participants of a group by appointment.
key_sources: Yeh M.-L., Chang B.-Y., Dai H.-D., & Chung M.-H. (2025). Effect of training program on evidence-based practice competencies in hospital nurses in Taiwan: A quasi-experimental study. The Journal of Nursing Research, 33(5), e412. https://doi.org/10.1097/jnr.0000000000000701
